claims.text: The feedstock is pre-alloyed AlCrFeNiSi powder with a conventional particle-size distribution for miniature-component additive manufacturing.
Laser energy density can be reduced by increasing scanning speed and/or decreasing laser power.
Lowering laser energy input in LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi will reduce thermal gradients during solidification.
Lower laser energy input will reduce the size and high-temperature extent of the melt pool.
Lower-energy processing will produce a more uniform and fine-grained microstructure.
Reduced melt-pool size and thermal gradients will diminish residual-stress accumulation.
Lower thermal input will prevent microstructural degradation that would otherwise compromise mechanical properties.
Lower-energy AlCrFeNiSi components will have significantly lower residual stresses than high-thermal-load LPBF controls.
Lower-energy AlCrFeNiSi components will have improved mechanical performance, including enhanced ductility and toughness, relative to high-thermal-load LPBF controls.
Conventional high-energy-density LPBF typically produces higher residual stresses, compromised microstructures, and degraded mechanical properties.
The proposed processing window uses a linear energy density below approximately 2.5–2.8 J/mm.
The intervention is intended for inert-atmosphere LPBF at ambient temperature and for components with dimensions of a few millimeters.
A NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy has previously been formed by selective laser melting as a single BCC solid solution at linear energy densities up to 2.83 J/mm.
The cited NbMoTaW material exhibited excellent microstructure, microhardness, and corrosion resistance relative to traditional superalloys.
The proposed benefits are limited to miniature LPBF components made from AlCrFeNiSi within the targeted processing window.
Larger geometries and other powder systems may require additional process adjustments.
Reducing energy input may decrease densification or impair interlayer bonding.

The hypothesis is falsified if lower-energy specimens show no statistically significant residual-stress reduction or microstructural refinement and have equal or inferior mechanical properties relative to the high-energy control.
